This update came out SIX MONTHS after the “Halloween” “2020” Update on May 8th, 2021. This update brought about two new towers, lots of patch notes, the Frost Invasion Event and unfortunately, more bugs and another long time span of no updates. MISCALLENOUS CHANGES Defense Rework - Defense was now changed to drop damage by a percentage instead of dropping it by a specific number based on the gamemode multiplier. This change made it so high burst damage towers, such as Ranger no longer had an advantage. It still stayed in the meta though. The defense dropping towers (Pyromancer, Electroshocker, Freezer, Frost Blaster) were also now more effective on dropping defense, since they also now dropped defense by a percentage. Splash Damage Rework - The explosion is now separated into two spheres, with the inner sphere dealing 100% of the stated damage while the outer sphere decreases damage linearly. This is nice, as towers dealing splash damage are now more consistent. Unfortunately, with the state of balancing of the game, almost every splash tower is very weak. matches.title: why golden crook boss is better than golden scout
matches.snippet: Golden Crook boss and golden scout both have been very good golden skins, up there at the top with mini. But recently, because i have both i wanted to see which one is better and for what reasons. Golden Crook Boss is better than golden scout If you want to see why golden scout is better than golden crook boss, scroll down. it is below and you will see it when you see it, it is in bold. To start, golden crook boss has a higher dps. from when you place it, it can do 2.5 damage per second, while golden scout does 1.33. and when you level it up one time, that damage is doubled and it can one shot everything up to heavy enemies. on the other side, golden scout does 1.33 till level 3, when it does 6.67. At max, golden crook boss does 60 dps to a 20 dps from max golden scout. Golden crook boss also has a faster fire rate, shooting about twice in the time golden scout would shoot until level 3. Continuing, if you farm correctly (6 level 1 farms) you can place a level 3 golden crook boss on wave 10, which effectively buys you a LOT of time to farm (until necromancer i'm pretty sure). On top of that, golden crook boss can summon golden guards, which have 25 health, 25 range, and 6.67 dps, around the same as golden scout at level 3. at max, these guards have more dps than a max golden scout, 33.33 damage, and have 55 health. Why Golden Scout is Better than Golden Crook Boss Golden scout

matches.title: Small Post
matches.snippet: Yeah TDS sucks and there's no point in making this post, but I don't care honestly. I'm not writing this for other people, I'm writing this for myself. Frankly, because I haven't written a long post in such a long time. Tower Defense Simulator is not a game where you strategize (you can but it's not really needed since like everything is soloable), but instead a game full of bugs, lag, horrible balancing, and developers who I think just... don't care about the community! (I mean seriously if they did then why is the game like how it is now) But that's not what I want to talk about. I want to talk about a few towers: the Assassin, the Golden Crook Boss, the Brawler, the Rocketeer, and the Mortar. Before we start. My opinions could be very off and incorrect, because me playing with people is close to zero, due to poor Roblox moderation and everything being soloable. I solo everything and have last played with people during the Ducky Revenge Event. I also don't want to argue with anyone, this is moreso me trying to understand people's views on towers more (because I truly cannot understand them). The first three are the ones I want to compare against. From what I've been seeing, people are saying that the Golden Crook Boss is better... How? Honestly, I played on Simplicity Remaster and the Assassins killed the Fallen Giant on Wave 16 just a little faster than the Golden Crook Boss

matches.title: Fallen Duo+ SPEEDRUN (Personal) Tower Rankings
matches.snippet: Yeah I know. I'm using a tierlist. But I include explanations for each placement, so take this like it's a tower ranking. Farm can be replaced with Golden Cowboy for the first player, but the the other players need Farm. Best Choices The best towers you can use for speedrunning Fallen, but can be replaced by inferior ones. Gladiator: Carries wave 0 ~ wave 38 since it has high DPS, low cost and infinite AoE. Accelerator: Self explanatory, just extremely high DPS. Engineer: Can be a Sub-DPS, a better choice than Golden Minigunner. Replaceable Towers that are slightly worse than the towers in Best Choices, but by no means bad. Golden Minigunner: High DPS, decent cost. Great for being a Sub-DPS. Decent job as a Main-DPS. Golden Crook Boss: Decent Sub-DPS. Can potentially stop leakings with guards. Ranking is NOT for starting tower. Golden Scout: Great starter tower. Viable Towers that are viable for speedrunning, but there are better options. Sledger: A decent Sub-DPS and minor support for mid to late wave. Turret: Can be used as a Sub-DPS for Trio+. matches.title: Towers you should get when you are starting out in TDS or you lost your account
matches.snippet: You joined the TDS community recently, and now you can't choose what tower to get. Fear nothing, because this post will help you know what towers to get when you are starting out. Since it is early game, you will of course have the 2 towers: Scout and Sniper. You also start off with some coins, but you should save the coins for later as most of the towers in early game are complete garbage. You should never buy towers that have golden skins (Except for Minigunner and Crook Boss, which is a Level 30 unlockable tower) Your first tower you want to prioritize on getting is Shotgunner. Shotgunner has very high damage on a single shot, reaching over 100+ damage in only 1.5 seconds on max. During the grind for Shotgunner, the only mode you want to play is Molten. No exceptions. Molten is by far the best and the 2nd best for grinding coins and EXP. Molten gives 4x more than Normal and is way easier than Normal mode. When you are ready to start grinding for Shotgunner, do not USE SNIPER. Sniper is overpriced and does the same DPS as Scout, which is way cheaper than Sniper. Because of how terrible Sniper is, you are better off spamming Scouts to deal with the early waves and for the first slow boss. matches.title: Tower Tierlist
matches.snippet: Here is my tierlist's viability ranking from S+ to F. S+ is the most useful choice to have on your deck and F is the worst choice to have on your deck. Only towers are covered in this ranking. Terms Raw Damage: Base damage of towers unaffected by Commander Buffed Damage: Improved damage of towers affected by Commander DPS: Damage Per Second, how much damage a tower can do within 1 second S+ Commander is an extremely solid tower that buffs towers through firerate which massively impacts the defending towers by 15% to a whopping 55%. Not only does this benefit fast firerate towers to do even more DPS, towers such as Ranger benefits massively, doing way more than damage than it is supposed. Towers that have high firerate are negatively impacted by the ROF bug, which means towers with slow firerate will deal way more damage than towers such as Accelerator and Minigunner. Overrall, having Commander in your deck is a must. S Ranger is an incredible damage dealer even at the first levels. Ranger simply has the highest raw damage out of all towers (excluding Military Base with collision damage), yielding the undefeated 300 damage per shot on max. Ranger is one of the best solo towers currently due to it being unaffected by stuns from shockwave and is massively unaffected by the infamous ROF Bug! matches.title: Is Golden Scout actually the best obtainable early game tower?
matches.snippet: I've recently unlocked the Golden Scout; naturally, I wanted to try it and use its early game potential in random lobbies. To my surprise, I didn't do too well for the early game. My strategy of course was to spam level 0s, this is because level 1 and 2 only slightly upgrade range and give HD, so spamming level 0s is the most cost efficient early game. I've run into problems with using the tower and I would like to compare it to another tower I have: the Golden Crook Boss. The Golden Crook Boss seems to do better in my experience and here is why: The first upgrade instantly doubles the damage, also one-shotting the quicks (or speedys I always get them confused) The second upgrade gives the golden crook, which is really good for dealing with the heftys on wave 7 and abnormal boss on wave 10 After getting level 2, I'm able to farm and get level 3 for wave 10 even in 4 player servers. Here are things the Golden Scout has going for it Somewhat better range More cost efficient at level 0 Can be placed instantly, unlike the Golden Crook Boss where you need to wait until wave 2 The problem I'm encountering is that by wave 7, Golden Scouts simply won't cut it. Now of course, I can just continue to spam these because of their insane cost-efficiency the moment they are placed, but there are problems with this. The most important issue: Space. matches.snippet: Part 20 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Release v1.8, and while it didn’t add any new towers, it brought about a lot of balance changes, and a new shield mechanic for the enemies, all of these things really shifted the meta. I’m going to uncover some miscellaneous changes first. MISCALLENOUS CHANGES Firerate Bug/ROF Bug - What even is the Firerate Bug? It is a bug that slows down the firerate of every tower and unit by 0.05s (0.025s for Level 4-5 Minigunner for some reason), prior to the Overhaul Update. This significantly affected fast-firing towers like the Minigunner, Ace Pilot and Turret. According to the wiki, the Firerate Bug has existed since the very release of the game. However, I just don’t think this was the case in Pre-MEGA, and early MEGA. It really only took notice around early 2020, but I have chosen to finally take the ROF Bug into account on these lists, since as mentioned, it started to take notice around this time and couldn't really be ignored anymore. This drops towers like the Minigunner (and Golden), Turret and Shredder on the ranking. Shield - This was a new mechanic that was added that enemies could have. matches.title: This one tower makes the other 5 look like a joke...
matches.snippet: Hi my name is Dat1TDEnjoyer, and I am essentially the superior older brother of CrazyTDfan. Out with intros, I'ma explain what this golden tower is and why it's fucking up the other ones. TL;DR nerf Golden Scout and buff Military Base, Crook Boss, Shotgunner, and Ace so all 5 can be on the same level. So basically, Golden towers are the most expensive. But were they designed to be the best at it's job? No! They were designed to be the 2nd best at their job, like a fun golden tower but not an OP one. Golden Minigunner, Golden Pyromancer, and Golden Cowboy are all good examples of this, being outclassed by the late game alliance(Ranger, Accel, Engineer), Mortar, and Farm respectively. Golden Crook Boss and Golden Soldier on the other hand, are outclassed by a literal Golden tower. This guy is Golden Scout. I am ok with it's OP early game if it's outclassed by a tower you get earlier on, but it deals 36 DPS at max level and can solo fallen with supports. What the fuck. This tower should only do something like 20-25 DPS at max, it's not supposed to be good for the mid game. It might need an early game price nerf, but if I say such shit, everyone is gonna scream. Why not nerf Gladiator, rebalance Ace to be more early game oriented, and buff Crook Boss, make Shotgunner's spread tighter on level 0, and clean up Military Base, in which these towers are the early game towers people use

matches.title: In defense of Mystery...
matches.snippet: Over the years, Mystery has been receiving unnecessary hate and the Breaker has been admired for replacing it. Is it really all bad, or do you suck at the game and try to excuse it? COMPARISON - People claiming "breaker makes you strategize," "breaker makes you not rely on single-target,' blah blah. Does it really? Well, no. Breaker can easily be killed by single target such as golden crook boss, brawler, golden soldier, normal soldier, normal crook boss. It seems to do horrible at doing its supposed job of making people strategize or plan-ahead. I've been in lobbies[trio & quad], and solo matches and just go without a plan and have never leaked nor struggled to breaker[the only splash I've seen are Jester, Pursuit missiles, and max ranger]. So much for making people "strategize" and use "splash damage," huh? Not only that, but you know it's going to spawn more breakers while being aware you have the DPS to kill them off. How about mystery? In modern TDS landscape[which is where I'm basing it off for both mystery & breaker], RNG isn't an issue. In juggernaut quest[Gilded Path], I was able to defeat an Abnormal Boss w/ 500 hp using 5 lvl. 2 Golden CB & 2 lvl. 2 elf camps. It got annihilated[keep in mind it had tank attribute], so what about abnormal bosses spawned by Mystery in regular games? They were playing the SFOTH event, which many people considered the hardest event in the game’s history. But right before Swordmaster got to the base, Blox activated Freezer’s ability, freezing Swordmaster in place. Then the Minigunners and Outlaws finished him off. “NO WAY”, said popcorn. “I'VE BEEN TRYING TO BEAT THIS EVENT FOR THE PAST FOUR HOURS!!” “u rlly need better time management”, said Blox. “Gladiator isnt even good” “it cant be that bad”, said popcorn. “also IVE SEEN U ONLINE FOR THE PAST SIX HOURS” They were teleported back to the Lobby. “alr bro im gonna test gladiator”, said popcorn. “r u gonna keep playing?” “ye until im at number # on the leaderboard”, said Blox. He was Level 122, the second highest level in the entire game. The only person who was higher than him was a player called Therobloxyo. He was Level 133, 11 levels higher than Blox. He continued to go into matches and won easily. Until… Blox’s soul was sucked into the game. However, he didn’t notice and continued to play. Eventually, his soul was split into small pieces. All of the towers in his Inventory gained a piece of his soul, bringing them all to life. They could now enter and exit the Inventory whenever they wanted, move around, and interact with players. “What is this?!”, said Freezer, moving his leg. “WOAH!! WE CAN MOVE!!”, said John excitedly. He ran in circles around the Inventory. Freezer, John, Minigunner, Outlaw, and Commander were teleported to the Sword Fight on the Heights map. Blox placed John down. “HI!!”, said John, waving at the players. “WHAT”, said the players in the chat. “how do u do that”, said Player 3. He placed down a John, but it functioned exactly like a normal tower. “What the..”, said Blox. He placed another John, but this one was a normal tower as well. Then he placed a Freezer. This one behaved like the first John. “Woah..”, said Freezer. He started to walk away. “THEY CAN MOVE?!”, said the players. “nice hax”, said Player 3. “i got this on vid” “GUYS!! FOCUS!!”, said Player 2. He pointed at Swordmaster. “I GOT THIS!”, said Freezer. He sprinted toward Swordmaster and tried to activate his ability. However, it didn’t work. Blox quickly placed a Level 5 Freezer and froze Swordmaster. They won and were taken to the Lobby. “That was odd.”, said Blox. Suddenly, he began to look around frantically. His heart was beating out of his chest. “W-what?! Why can’t I.. what is going on?!? Am I… IN THE GAME?!?” Meanwhile, the towers were having fun in the Inventory with their newfound ability to move. “Hey guys.. what is that?”, said Commander. He was pointing at a bright door in the center of the Inventory. “Who’s gonna go through it?”, said Scout. “Three… two.. one.. NOT IT!!”, they all said at the same time. They all looked at Crook Boss. “You were the last person who said it!”, Demoman told Crook Boss. “Wait, I don’t want to!”, said Crook Boss. “Take one for the team. We’ll be right behind you!”, John said right before pushing Crook Boss straight through it. Crook Boss reappeared in the LOBBY next to Blox. “Crook Boss?”, said Blox. Freezer, John, Commander, Pyromancer, Scout, and the rest of the towers went through the door as well. “I told you we were right behind you!”, said John. “Why is this thing only happening to me…?”, Blox asked. “What’s wrong?”, asked Pyromancer. “How do I get out of this place?”, Blox asked. “What’s wrong with it?”, asked Scout. **Wait, if I’m in this game, what would happen if I kill a tower..?** Blox killed Pyromancer. (50 Health, 4 Damage, 0.188s Firerate, 18 Range, detects Hidden enemies) No longer spawns Body Guards 2. Crook Boss got a massive rework, and for the better. While the cost efficiency of the Crook Boss itself got worse, due to much higher prices, it is backed up by the fact that its minions, more specifically, the Tommy Goons are significantly stronger and more reliable than the previous Body Guards, due to their much higher DPS, shorter spawnrate and hidden detection, only at the cost of way less range. The Pistol Goons are also very helpful for assisting in early-game with their relatively fast spawnrate, and while they do have flying detection, their DPS is just a tad too weak to be used for Balloons in Hardcore mode. At Level 4, with a DPS of 55.56, plus Tommy Goon 2’s 21.28 DPS, plus the 2 Pistol Goons’ 3.3 DPS, that totals to 80.14 DPS for $16,600, which is really good for an intermediate tower. The DPS can also be much higher if you can stack the units, which can be easily done since they have a much faster spawnrate and stop while attacking. Obviously, this is just on paper, and the units can easily be wiped out in late-game. Overall, Crook Boss is a lot better in early-mid game thanks to its stronger units, and it is a bit more serviceable for late-game now with a higher DPS and placement limit. Crook Boss moves up from high C tier to low-mid B tier. Unfortunately, you cannot place it at the start of a match anymore due to the higher placement cost, and again, the tower itself has worse cost efficiency due to much higher prices, but being backed up by significantly stronger minions. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: Part 26 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Overhaul v1.3, the Frost Invasion Update. This update came out SIX MONTHS after the “Halloween” “2020” Update on May 8th, 2021. This update brought about two new towers, lots of patch notes, the Frost Invasion Event and unfortunately, more bugs and another long time span of no updates. MISCALLENOUS CHANGES Defense Rework - Defense was now changed to drop damage by a percentage instead of dropping it by a specific number based on the gamemode multiplier. This change made it so high burst damage towers, such as Ranger no longer had an advantage. It still stayed in the meta though. The defense dropping towers (Pyromancer, Electroshocker, Freezer, Frost Blaster) were also now more effective on dropping defense, since they also now dropped defense by a percentage. Splash Damage Rework - The explosion is now separated into two spheres, with the inner sphere dealing 100% of the stated damage while the outer sphere decreases damage linearly. This is nice, as towers dealing splash damage are now more consistent. Unfortunately, with the state of balancing of the game, almost every splash tower is very weak. NEW TOWERS Toxic Gunner - Unlocked from beating the “Halloween” “2020” Event, the Toxic Gunner fired in bursts, similar to the Soldier. These shots apply slowdown to enemies, while also dealing damage over time. However, it was extremely buggy on release. The slowdown was PERMANENT. Every enemy hit would be slowed down by FIFTY PERCENT, and best of all, the slowdown affected MAJOR BOSSES such as Void Reaver, Frost Spirit and Creator.. Really, the only problem Toxic Gunner had was no hidden detection, which barely matters when you make every game a free win. It was the main reason why the Frost Invasion Event was so easy to win, contrary to what the developers stated (in fact it made the event soloable). Toxic Gunner easily lands on S tier, #1. It was really that broken. How did this get past testing? Sledger - Unlocked from beating the Frost Invasion Event, the Sledger was another melee tower, attacking enemies by bashing them with its hammer. These swings could miss enemies and only hit one target, so Sledger wasn’t that good at early game. Level 3+ is when things get good. It is now able to freeze targets, multiple of them. The freeze time was always 2 seconds, not restricted by enemy size unlike Freezer and Frost Blaster. At Level 4+, frozen enemies would receive twice the damage, so Sledger was actually pretty good at defending by itself, being excellent at crowd control, and it is just much more effective at actually freezing enemies than Freezer or Frost Blaster ever could, so it was a very vital tower for Hidden Wave. Really, the only thing Sledger struggled against were hidden enemies as it didn’t have hidden detection, major bosses, which was made worse by Sledger’s low placement limit of six. It lands a spot on high A tier. BALANCE CHANGES Freezer Level 3 Defense dropping: 1 -> 5% Level 5 Defense dropping: 2 -> 10% Frost Blaster Level 3 Defense dropping: 1 -> 5% Just the global change every tower with this ability got. Both towers still suck I fear. They remain in E tier. Militant Militant now has ammo, when it runs out of ammo, or does not detect any enemies for a while, it will start reloading. Level 0 Cost: $1,200 -> 750 Damage: 2 -> 1 Firerate: 0.43s -> 0.23s Range: 12 -> 10 Now has 18 ammo, Reload Time of 2.5s Level 1 Damage: 2 -> 1 Firerate: 0.43s -> 0.23s Range: 14 -> 12 Level 2 Damage: 2 -> 1 Firerate: 0.43s -> 0.23s Range: 15 -> 13 Level 3 Damage remains at 2 Firerate: 0.23s -> 0.155s Range: 15 -> 13 Now has 30 ammo Level 4 Damage remains at 4 Firerate: 0.23s -> 0.155s Range: 15 -> 14 Level 5 removed The developers said this would make Militant “better”. Guess what? It did the exact opposite. The ammo system just doesn’t work and is such a HUGE hindrance, especially now that the tower’s range was even worse, and the reload time of 2.5s is just miserable. The DPS is already too little for its cost, except for Level 0. The DPS was literally LESS than Medic’s, a support tower. Militant goes down from low C tier to E tier, now among one of the worst towers in the game. Medic Level 5 BUG: Cleansing ability no longer removes stuns from towers, due to the new stun system. Well, guess what. Medic’s main use is basically redundant now. While it can heal the base health, that ability is honestly just useless, and its DPS is way too low. Goes down from high C tier to E tier, now among one of the worst towers. Ace Pilot Ace Pilot’s bombs now aim directly to where its targeted enemy was last at, as opposed to straight down for Levels 2-4 Ace Pilot now has to take off from its runaway, when placed down, and when upgraded to Level 3 and 5. BUG: No longer immune to stuns and freeze. Level 0 Cost: $650 -> $500 Level 2 Splash Damage: 12 -> 10 Explosion Range

On top of that, golden crook boss can summon golden guards, which have 25 health, 25 range, and 6.67 dps, around the same as golden scout at level 3. at max, these guards have more dps than a max golden scout, 33.33 damage, and have 55 health. This update was most notable for releasing the Pirate skins series, just like most of the updates before it that I skipped. But unlike the past updates, it also brought about a long list of balance changes. Let's dive in. BALANCE CHANGES Demoman Level 0 Firerate: 3.008s -> 2.758s Range: 8 -> 9 Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $100 -> $50 Firerate: 2.658s -> 2.508s Range remains at 10 Level 2 Upgrade Cost: $525 -> $450 Firerate: 2.658s -> 2.508s Range remains at 10 Level 3 Firerate remains at 1.508s Range remains at 12 Level 4 Firerate remains at 1.208s Range remains at 14 Hidden detection added Demoman got a very small buff, slightly improving its firerate and reducing its price at the early levels. Level 3 and 4 are still the same, except for Level 4 getting hidden detection, something Demoman has lacked for a very long time now. However, these buffs barely matter, with the firerate still being slow, hindering its early-game performance, and Level 4 is far too expensive to be used for early-game hidden detection. Remains at the same spot in C tier. Crook Boss Level 0 Cost: $650 -> $450 Firerate: 0.808s -> 0.758s Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $300 -> $250 Firerate: 0.808s -> 0.758s Now spawns Body Guard unit

BALANCE CHANGES Demoman Level 0 Firerate: 3.008s -> 2.758s Range: 8 -> 9 Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $100 -> $50 Firerate: 2.658s -> 2.508s Range remains at 10 Level 2 Upgrade Cost: $525 -> $450 Firerate: 2.658s -> 2.508s Range remains at 10 Level 3 Firerate remains at 1.508s Range remains at 12 Level 4 Firerate remains at 1.208s Range remains at 14 Hidden detection added Demoman got a very small buff, slightly improving its firerate and reducing its price at the early levels. Level 3 and 4 are still the same, except for Level 4 getting hidden detection, something Demoman has lacked for a very long time now. However, these buffs barely matter, with the firerate still being slow, hindering its early-game performance, and Level 4 is far too expensive to be used for early-game hidden detection. Remains at the same spot in C tier. Crook Boss Level 0 Cost: $650 -> $450 Firerate: 0.808s -> 0.758s Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $300 -> $250 Firerate: 0.808s -> 0.758s Now spawns Body Guard unit (moved from Level 2) Added Max Units of 1 Level 2 Firerate: 0.808s -> 0.558s Body Guard unit Spawnrate: 60s -> 45s Level 3 Upgrade Cost: $1,500 -> $2,000 Firerate: 0.208s -> 0.158s Range: 13 -> 12 Increases Max Units to 2 Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $9,000 -> $8,000 Damage: 7 -> 5 Firerate: 0.158s -> 0.108s Range remains at 15 Body Guards 2 unit Spawnrate: 45s -> 40s Increases Max Units to 3 Crook Boss got a nice buff, having cheaper prices (with Level 3 only getting slightly more expensive), and slightly higher DPS. The Body Guard being spawnable on an earlier level means it helps more in early-game, but the units are still quite weak and die easily in mid-late game. Overall, Crook Boss now fares much better against early-mid game, but still struggles in late-game with its 4 placement limit and small range. It moves up to high-C tier. Warden Placement Limit of 20 added. Level 0 Swingrate: 1.208s -> 1.108s Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $350 -> $250 Swingrate: 1.008s -> 0.908s Level 2 Swingrate remains at 0.808s Level 3 Damage: 30 -> 40 (Crit Damage: 45 -> 60) Swingrate remains at 0.808s Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $13,500 -> $14,500 Damage: 80 -> 100 (Crit Damage: 120 -> 150) Swingrate remains at 0.808s Shield stun block cooldown: 5s -> 0.25s Warden also got a buff. The faster swingrate at the earlier levels means it leaks less enemies on early game, and the higher damage at the later levels simply mean more DPS, and with the cooldown of the stun block passive ability being really short now, it's now practically immune to stuns. It's still not that great in early-game due to its lack of AoE as a melee tower, and obviously short range. It definitely got better in mid-late game though, and it can still stun enemies, which helps. Also, its placement limit of 20 is kind of pointless, which is by far the highest placement limit out of every tower who has one. It is literally the total tower placement limit in quads. Warden goes up from mid B tier to low A tier. Accelerator Damage values no longer fluctuate. Burst Time stat replaced with Overcharge stat. Level 0 Hidden detection removed, moved to Level 1. Level 1 Damage: 14 -> 15 Level 2 Damage: 14 -> 15 Overcharge: 280 -> 375 Level 3 Damage remains at 25 Overcharge: 425 -> 625 Level 4 Damage: 36 -> 45 Overcharge: 1,080 -> 1,650 Level 5 Upgrade Cost: $30,000 -> $34,000 Damage remains at 50 Range: 22.5 -> 20 Overcharge remains at 3,000 Accelerator at Level 0-4 got a buff, with higher damage and overcharge. Level 5 did receive a small nerf to its range and increased price, but it barely matters, having the same DPS. Accelerator remains at #3. Back in v1.7.0, both Pyromancer and Golden Pyromancer received stat changes, but in doing so, Golden Pyromancer now almost has the exact same stats as Level 0-2 regular Pyromancer, making it kind of worthless. Golden Pyromancer only costed $100-150 less, with the only real advantage being automatic hidden detection, Level 3-5 were still significantly better though. This buff aims to fix those issues. The first three are the ones I want to compare against. From what I've been seeing, people are saying that the Golden Crook Boss is better... How? Honestly, I played on Simplicity Remaster and the Assassins killed the Fallen Giant on Wave 16 just a little faster than the Golden Crook Boss. The Golden Crook Boss's units, at least to me, are frankly useless. The only Tower I like to use that has units I actually like is the Mercenary Base. Speaking about that, the Mercenary Base may or may not take shorter to grind for than the Golden Crook Boss, though I'm unsure, as I'm way past Level 150 and have all Golden Towers so... I can't confirm anything. What's so good about the Golden Crook Boss? Now I got a reply to a comment I made on the Golden Crook Boss page where somebody straight up just insulted me for no reason (wasn't even talking about the tower itself I was joking about the image in the infobox). You can view the image below: Firstly, I just wanna say that I don't see the Golden Crook Boss seen in the TDS videos I've seen (nor the Assassin but I have seen the Brawler used sometimes), but I barely watch TDS, since most content not made by the Platter Bros or like propellars or CORSO is boring. Secondly, I wanna say that the Golden Crook Boss, from what I've seen, kind of falls off in Late Game. Thirdly, you know who else has good cost efficiency? The Assassin. With $59.15 COST EFFICIENCY AT MAX LEVEL!!! You hear how crazy that sounds?! 59!!! Fourthly, many towers have Hidden Detection so that point is redundant, and the Flying Detection is kind of just... bad. I mean you got the Ranger, the Gatling Gun (which I wouldn't recommend using but still), the Electroshocker, the Commander, the Mercenary Base, the Necromancer, and other towers I think are better with Flying Detection. Lastly, no. I am not ragebaiting. I have like... never rage baited. Please don't try to argue with me and scream at me saying the Golden Crook Boss is good. Unless I get points better than THAT on how the Golden Crook Boss is like apparently outstanding or whatever, yeah, I'm sticking to my Archer, Assassin, Golden Cowboy, and other towers. Oh yeah, also, the Golden Cowboy can give you money... Golden Crook Boss can't. Oh well, yeah, the only good Golden Tower is the Golden Cowboy (maybe the Golden Minigunner too?). Next, I wanna ask a question. Were the balancers taking the Brawler into account when buffing the Assassin? Yeah, the Assassin has 40 less DPS. Except there's one problem... The Brawler has a Placement Limit of 6. The Assassin? None! No Placement Limit! Nada! Mind you, the Brawler takes like 4 games of the objectively 2nd most boring gamemode in the entire game (right behind PvP). The Assassin? Oh yeah, it only takes 3 games of Easy mode, 2 games of Casual, Intermediate, and Molten, and 1 game of Fallen. What the hell? Should've only gotten a small buff on Level 0 to be able to get past Wave 1 in Fallen, but that's it. This buff is WAY too big. I hope the Assassin gets nerfed in the next update. Because if I had to choose between the Assassin or the Brawler... I'm going for the Assassin. I will say this. The PvP stats for these towers are pretty good. They should be transferred over to the regular game, as I think this is good balancing. Though! I've used neither towers in PvP, sooo... I might be a little lost on this. I haven't tried it yet! But if I had to guess, probably not, since he's kind of expensive compared to the Assassin, costing $10,250 more to max out. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: Part 23 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Release v1.12, the Hardcore BETA Update. I have chosen to do this post separately from Overhaul v1.0 as it contains some slight differences. This update added 2 new towers, 1 new golden skin, and changed the stats of pretty much every tower, mostly for the worse. I will also uncover certain miscellaneous changes. But before all that though, I feel like stating why this update was such a fiasco. First off, the update was already delayed. It was meant to release on August 21st, but it was delayed to a week later to August 28th, due to some issues. But was the delay enough? Well… On August 28th 2020, 3:00 PM EST(?), the live event would start. This live event would begin with the screen going black, with the following text being displayed: “...”“I feel it… the end…”“[???]: The end is only the beginning” After this, the screen would return to normal and the skybox in the lobby would change. Purple orbs would begin to fall from the sky, with your goal being to avoid them for 1 minute and 30 seconds. No matter if you survived or not, an animation would play after 1 minute and 30 seconds, where spinning purple light would come out of the eye in the door, and shortly after other parts of the turn would turn neon purple. The eye would then become a black hole that pulled in multiple parts of the lobby and players. However, the screen just turned black, and the game was shut down for maintenance a few minutes later. You received a badge for participating in this live event. After the game came back up, the update was rolled around. However, it was a disastrous mess of bugs. Many towers had wrong stats, many skins were just removed from player’s inventories, data loss and it was just so obvious that the update was rushed. It was not ready even with the delay. The game went on another maintenance, the developers apologized, then reverted the game back to Release v1.11, with a button to click on top of the lobby to access Hardcore BETA. Anyways, after all that, let’s uncover the important miscellaneous changes. MISCALLENEOUS CHANGES Firerate Bug effectiveness decreased: Went from slowing down the firerate of every tower and unit by 0.05s to 0.03s. Global placement limit changes: Solo placement limit increased from 30 to 40, Duo placement limit increased from 20 to 30, Trio placement limit increased from 20 to 25, 5+ players placement limit decreased from 20 to 16 Splash Damage equation reworked Shield attribute replaced with Shield Health Defense mechanic added for enemies Wave Bonuses were massively buffed, many enemies were massively nerfed, game just became overall easier NEW TOWERS Accelerator - Unlocked from buying it in the shop with 2,500 Gems, which is a new currency obtained from Hardcore mode. Once an enemy is in range of the Accelerator, it will charge up its laser and focus on it until the target is killed or leaves the Accelerator’s range. After its burst time is over, it will then wave its hand, indicating a cooldown, then charge up again after the cooldown ends. Do note that the Accelerator does not always deal the stated damage, with the actual being 70-100% of what the stated damage indicates. As for the stats of the Accelerator.. Its high DPS was the main standing point, being the highest out of every tower in the game without buffs. However, its charge-up and cooldown were quite massive problems. It could very easily lock onto a high HP enemy and let many other fast enemies pass by, and its range is only okay at best, being 19 at max level. It’s still a really good late-game tower, being nearly the same price as Outlaw, having a slightly lower placement limit of 8, and being much, much better at handling hordes. Outlaw was still much more reliable and consistent though, and Accelerator’s DPS was hindered quite a lot by the ROF Bug. The Accelerator gets a spot on the low S tier. Mecha Base - This tower was actually added to the game on January 12th 2020, but it was only accessible to staff. On this update, it was added to the shop and you could buy it for 3,500 Gems. Mecha Base was pretty much just a stronger Military Base, sending out units every several seconds, which were much much more powerful than Military Base’s units. It dealt splash damage with missiles starting at Level 1, but they were quite weak. The tower was extremely buggy though, but in its own favor. First off, it used Medic’s upgrade costs. Mecha Base still had its own placement cost of $5,000, but every upgrade used Medic’s upgrade costs, which to say were extremely cheap for the DPS the tower dealt would be an understatement. At Level 4+, it had a massive range of 100, easily being able to cover the longest maps. C-Tier: Demoman, Scout, Sniper, Hunter, Archer, Cowboy, Pyromancer, Golden Pyromancer, Golden Cowboy, Crook Boss, Toxic Gunner, Executioner. Demoman, the lowest of C-Tier. The only reason this guy isn't in D-Tier is because it's able to do alright damage compared to the other towers in the lower tiers. Scout, for being the starter tower, it can be able to handle quite a lot. But like the Demoman, Scout can't handle massive hordes of bosses. Sniper, the starter cliff tower. Does some good damage, but with a cost of shooting slow and not being able to defend off hordes. The only reason why it's above Scout is because it has high range, countering the slow shooting. And its high damage, being able to take down a Normal/Abnormal Boss in just a few shots. Hunter, a good tower for costing under $1,000 just to unlock the tower. With it being one of the only ground towers to hit flying enemies. But other towers do what Hunter does, just a lot better. Archer, an alright tower with decent damage and range. With it being able to hit multiple enemies whilst making them take fire damage, it's safe to say this tower is a C-Tier. The only reason why it isn't higher is because other towers manage to do what archer does, just better. Cowboy. Once being an amazing tower, now fallen down to C-Tier. Now, even though it's able to generate money, by the time you get cowboy you would already have Farm, a much better tower than Cowboy. Pyromancer, being able to do 56 damage (in total). The pyromancer is an all around decent tower, being able to remove defense. And being able to do bonus damage to enemies in the (removed) Frost Invasion event. Golden Pyromancer, just like the original Pyromancer, but better. Ever since its rebalance it hasn't been holding up as well. But doing more gives it an advantage. Golden Cowboy. Once being one of the best towers in the game, being actual meta and better than farm, has fallen from its place. Now, it is only seen as a slightly better cowboy. With higher damage, more money. But it will never go back to what it originally was. Crook Boss, being one of the only towers to spawn units. Decent damage, good firerate, and even more damage with its units. This tower is overall pretty good and is an option for early and mid game defense. Toxic Gunner, a powerful tower, being able to slow down enemies whilst doing poison damage. It has a burst count like Soldier, while having advantages to make it not be a complete clone. Now, controversial take but, Executioner isn't that good for a tower. Yes, the 80 damage is good and all. But what do you really need it for? Yes, it can shred enemies and bounce off of them. But other towers do that better. Gladiator can hit multiple enemies, but since it has more DPS and variety on how you use it, it's better than executioner. But it is still a good tower, with its damage and all. It was most notable for the Duck Hunt Event, obviously. Aside from that, it only added one new tower, and not much balance changes, as such, there weren’t that many changes made to the ranking, so I will also uncover Modern v1.2.2, the Golden Perks Update, which came out on May 13th. NEW TOWERS Engineer - Unlockable from the shop with 4,500 Gems, almost twice as Accelerator’s unlock cost. The Engineer was obviously “based off” of the Engineer from TF2, building sentries. It required to fill up a Scrap Meter, which it did so by just doing damage, and after it was filled up, it would build a Sentry. There could be a maximum of 2-4 Sentries per Engineer, depending on the level. As for the stats, the Engineer only cost $750 to place down, so you can actually use it for early-game defense. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: Part 31 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Modern v1.2.0, the Duck Hunt Update, which came out on April 17th 2022. It was most notable for the Duck Hunt Event, obviously. Aside from that, it only added one new tower, and not much balance changes, as such, there weren’t that many changes made to the ranking, so I will also uncover Modern v1.2.2, the Golden Perks Update, which came out on May 13th. NEW TOWERS Engineer - Unlockable from the shop with 4,500 Gems, almost twice as Accelerator’s unlock cost. The Engineer was obviously “based off” of the Engineer from TF2, building sentries. It required to fill up a Scrap Meter, which it did so by just doing damage, and after it was filled up, it would build a Sentry. There could be a maximum of 2-4 Sentries per Engineer, depending on the level. As for the stats, the Engineer only cost $750 to place down, so you can actually use it for early-game defense. It also had a deadzone range where it could not attack nor build sentries, but it was very small so it just didn’t matter. The Engineer itself dealt low DPS though, and the Sentries at the time didn’t have hidden nor flying detection, but the Engineer did. It was the first tower to be upgradeable to 6 Levels. It dealt lots of DPS for its cost, having a combined DPS of 454.5, which is the highest possible DPS in the game without buffs, but that’s only when all sentries are built. And unfortunately, the Sentries being units, are not affected by buffs such as firerate and range buffs, so that’s the maximum DPS you’re getting from them. And they can also be destroyed by enemy attacks that deal damage, such as stomps. These made them very vulnerable against bosses and just not reliable as a DPS tower in the long-run, but it still works on early-mid game. The Engineer only gets placed on A tier. 6 days later, to address this issue, Engineer would receive a change, where its sentries now have a bubble shield at Level 4+, which protects them from damage while active. It would only go inactive when the Engineer was stunned, so you could easily pair it with a Medic to instantly repair the shields. This was a buff that the Engineer very much needed, and places it on S tier, #4. BALANCE CHANGES Shotgunner Damage of each bullet is no longer decreased by 50% with each pierce. It now deals full damage to the first two enemies, and half damage to the last enemy. Pierce is no longer based on how high the damage of Shotgunner is, all levels now have a pierce of 2. (3 Max Hits) Level 0 Cost: $500 -> $400 Damage: 1x6 -> 2x6 Spread of 80 added. It can now hit multiple enemies right off the bat, and just deal more DPS, making it much better for early game. The later levels now also dish out overall more DPS than it used to, and got even better for crowd-control. The new Level 4 has slightly better stats than the old Level 5, with more DPS, but costing slightly more. It now has 1 less max hit, but with 2 more range. Shotgunner moves up from high B tier to low A tier. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: Part 40 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're diving into v1.9.0, the Lunar Overture Update, which came out on October 28th, 2023. It was most notable for adding the Lunar Overture Event. But aside from that, it came with another long list of balance changes, and finally new towers after 10 months. Let’s dive in. NEW TOWERS Necromancer - This tower was actually added 3 days later on v1.9.0g. It was unlocked from the shop with 1,800 Gems. The Necromancer was quite a complicated tower. At early levels, it fires magic bolts, which at Level 1+ , can pierce through enemies. At Level 4, this is replaced by a beam fired from its book, which are not projectiles and can hit up to 4 enemies at once. That’s not what the tower really is about though. It has a “Soul Meter” stat which it fills up by simply damaging enemies, when it becomes full, it creates a gravestone near it on the path, having a maximum of 6. It can destroy its gravestones using its “Raise the Dead” ability, which periodically stops it from attacking, these gravestones will then summon random units, and any units spawned by the previous use of the ability will be killed. At Level 4, these gravestones also explode when destroyed, dealing damage. The tower had very expensive prices, costing $45,000 to max out, and it had a placement limit of 3. At Level 0-1, it just spawns Skeletons, which just collide with enemies, having a low amount of health. At Level 1, it can now spawn Sword Skeletons, which deal melee damage. At Level 2, Skeletons are upgraded to Giant Skeletons, having way more health, and Sword Skeletons are upgraded to Skeleton Knights. At Level 3, Giant Skeletons are upgraded to Hallow Guards, and Necromancer can now summon an Executioner Skeleton, having long range, and throwing an axe to deal quick ticks of damage, which then returns after 4 seconds, and it also had a lot of health. As for the overall stats of the Necromancer, its single-target DPS was abysmal for its cost, but that doesn’t really matter, because it is able to hit multiple enemies, so even the Necromancer itself deals with hordes well. The skeletons themselves are much more powerful though when stacked, especially the Executioner Skeleton. The tower is best used for late-game since the early units are very weak. But honestly, the tower is just… unreliable. The skeletons spawned by the ability are completely random every time, and the ability also kills the previously spawned skeletons and periodically stops the Necromancer from attacking, and even then the skeletons die easily when not used right. Don’t get me wrong, the tower is fun to use, especially and can be strong when used right at max level, but it’s just not really reliable. It lands a spot on high C tier. Jester - Added on November 12th, 2023, along with Act 3, the final act of the event, with the Jester being the tower reward for beating it. It threw a bomb at enemies, which obviously dealt splash damage, and it gets two bombs at Level 4. The tower was mainly focused on debuffs, with different types of bombs providing different effects.. The first type of bomb, being the fire bomb which is unlocked at Level 0, obviously deals burn damage, and surprisingly the tower’s DPS is really good for its cost with these fire bombs, and it still deals hordes really well with its splash damage and high burn damage. At Level 2, it can now use ice bombs, which freezes affected enemies for 2 seconds, but decreases Jester’s DPS a lot. At Level 3, it can now use poison bombs, which leaves an acid puddle upon exploding that lasts for 10 seconds, and dealing damage-over-time to enemies, though its single-target DPS was really low and the bombs don’t even splash damage. At Level 4, it can now use confusion bombs, which causes enemies to walk backwards for 3 seconds, being an 8 second cooldown after for each Jester. However, the confusion bombs affected MAJOR BOSSES, such as Fallen King, Nuclear Monster, and Void Reaver, overall making the tower extremely potent with stalling and debuffing enemies. Use fire bombs for DPS, and the ice and confusion bombs for stalling (but NEVER use ice with fire now due to a new rework for the debuff system). The confusion bombs being able to affect major bosses just trivialized the game. (feels like pre-bugfix Toxic Gunner all over again). In fact, it made soloing Hardcore possible again after several months. Even outside of its stalling and debuffing use, the tower was good for early-game with its high splash damage and very cheap cost, only costing $9,350 to max out, and if that wasn’t enough, it also had instant hidden detection at Level 0, and it can be even used as early-game defense in Hardcore since it had lead penetration with its splash damage. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: This tier list will go over how good the towers are, from their DPS and price to how well they fare in the three stages of a regular TDS game from S tier to F tier. This tier list does not include restricted towers like War Machine or Void Miner, or towers that are the legacy version of an already existing tower like John or Outlaw, but does include Mecha Base. Keep in mind that this tier list is my opinion, so if a tower is not where you want it to be, I'm sorry, I didn't research the tower enough. Keep in mind that this is pretty inaccurate once we get down to Tiers C-F. Starting from S Tier, we've got... S TIER - FARM - No one expected this. Farm is, without a doubt, the best tower in the game, and for a good reason. Accelerator, Golden Minigunner, and Ranger are pretty overpowered damage-dealing towers, but the main drawback with them is that they're expensive as hell, especially Accelerator and Ranger. And what gives money better than our main potato hero? That's right, the Farm. ACCELERATOR - Although annoying to grind, this tower is worth it. In the early-game (Wave 1 to 22), this tower can be useful for when your Golden Scout/Soldier or Gladiators can't kill Shadows/Fallens quick enough. And in late-game (35-40 or 45-50 in Hardcore) it's your main damage dealer because of its insanely high 325 DPS plus the fact that it has Hidden Detection. The main drawback though, is that at Level 0-4, it charges pretty slow, and also it's expensive is hell. The latter can be almost negated by a Level 5 DJ Booth and Farms, but for the former... not as much. It's still usable on Level 0-4 though, and it definitely sits as one of the most overpowered towers in the game. COMMANDER - The narrator of the game, and also a necessity for every mode. When you've only got one Commander, you should be conserving Call to Arms for the more difficult struggles your team is facing. But with three and a good CTA chainer, the game's practically over. The firerate decrease makes your Accelerators and Golden Minigunners a force to be reckoned with, and you can get that 45-55% firerate decrease infinitely if you chain properly. One of the best support towers, and for good reason. DJ BOOTH - Your Accelerators and Rangers will benefit massively. The range buff is useful, it lets towers attack sooner than without the range buff, but the discount buff is an absolute godsend. Your Accelerators and Rangers are two of the most expensive towers in the entire game, and the DJ Booth's discount buff helps them massively. Easy S Tier. GOLDEN MINIGUNNER - A golden experience. It's the Turret, but it has no placement limit and it's less expensive. It's the same as Minigunner at Levels 0-2, but at Level 3-4 is where it starts to get its damage boost. It's useful for Abnormal Boss if the Gladiators/Golden Scouts/Golden Soldiers can't kill it quick, and it's really useful against Wave 25 on Hardcore Mode where there are three Shadow Bosses to deal with, and it can certainly do good on early-game with its 120 DPS. GLADIATOR - The Gladiator is on S Tier simply because it does well on all three stages in a TDS game. It's excellent on early-game, it's good on mid-game, and it still does well on late-game because of Warrior's Call decreasing your swingrate with the continuous CTA chain along with its 80 DPS. MECHA BASE - Oh hey! It's the Military Base, but better! Widely considered to be one of the best towers in the game, the Mecha Base shines high in the DPS field. It has the highest health for a single unit, the highest range in the game, and one of the lowest firerates in the game. The problems are that it doesn't have Hidden Detection, its spawnrate is still the same from Level 0-5 as a Level 0 Military Base's, and you can't decrease its firerate with Commander's CTA. Because the main reason I put Medic on A Tier is because the only thing that carries it to A Tier is only used on either the last wave or the waves where a major boss spawns. Yes, the only thing that made it A Tier is only used on late-game. LATE-GAME. That's just my only vendetta against it. I can sense the potential this tower has, but because there are a limited amount of enemies that can stun more than one, no, two towers, I'm putting it on A Tier. RANGER - This tower got nerfed, but it actually didn't. The lack of Hidden Detection, its high firerate, and how expensive it is puts the Ranger at A Tier instead of S Tier. It's still a good tower though, the 300 damage and very high range makes it a great tower. GOLDEN SCOUT - The prince of early-defense, and nothing else. Like, that's just it. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: Part 43 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 NEW TOWERS Trapper - Unlocked from the shop with 3,000 coins (the first tower to be just buyable from the shop with coins in 4 years), the Trapper would lay its traps on the nearby path around its range every few seconds depending on its firerate when there are no enemies in range, but will directly attack an enemy by throwing its traps if there are in its range. It has a maximum of 5 traps at Level 0, increasing by one every level, being a maximum of 9 at Level 4. There were three different types which the Trapper can switch to depending on the set trap the player set. The first type is the spike trap unlocked at Level 0, they have a set amount of health, which when decreased to zero makes them disappear. It can hit many enemies as long as it still has health, and it can deal more damage than its health, as the damage it deals to an enemy is the same as its full health, but an enemy’s defense can decrease it. The second type is the landmine unlocked at Level 3, which explodes upon an enemy steps on it, dealing splash damage to all enemies caught in the radius, as well as burning them, also decreasing an enemy’s defense by 7.5% per every tick with a maximum of 50% at Level 4. The third one is the bear trap unlocked at Level 4. Unlike the previous two traps, it can only hit a single enemy, but deals more damage. Upon contact, it stuns the enemy hit for 3 seconds. With this info provided, it seems like the Trapper is an amazing tower fulfilling different roles. The spike traps are good for early-game, the landmines are good for crowds, and the bear traps are good for stalling. Unfortunately, it takes a very long time to build up all of its traps, so you’d have to place it at the back of the map, so prepare for your matches to take very long in early-game, even then there are much better options for early-game, and its cost-for-DPS efficiency at later levels is absolutely atrocious. The main problem with Trapper is that it just doesn’t work in TDS’ core design, past early-game, Trapper is really only good for catching leaks, and if enemies leak past your main DPS spot, you just panic and lose the game. If you leak enemies a lot, you should just bring a much better tower to not leak enemies in the first place. Trapper was just not very practical to use during its early stages of release, so Trapper lands a spot on E tier, one of the worst towers in the game, even worse than Scout. BALANCE CHANGES Shotgunner Level 0 Firerate: 2.508s -> 2.108s Spread: 80 -> 60 Level 1 Firerate: 1.808s -> 1.508s Spread: 80 -> 60 Level 2 Firerate: 1.808s -> 1.508s Spread: 60 -> 50 Lead penetration added Level 3 Upgrade Cost: $3,500 -> $3,650 Firerate: 1.508s -> 1.308s Spread remains at 50 Removes lead penetration due to a bug Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $10,000 -> $9,000 Damage: 6x12 -> 7x10 Firerate: 1.008s -> 0.908s Spread: 50 -> 40 Lead penetration added Shotgunner has received no changes for a long time now, so this was quite due. Anyways, the buff was very impactful, now with an improved firerate, it has slightly more DPS, and more importantly, it leaks less enemies, as well as lead penetration, giving it a real use for Hardcore in early-game. (dont upgrade to Level 3 in Hardcore though) It is arguably the best early-game tower now, maybe even better than Gladiator and Golden Scout. Shotgunner is way easier to use than Gladiator, and way better value than Golden Scout, while being able to pierce through 3 enemies at once, the same as Gladiator. Of course, Shotgunner still suffers from its short range. Shotgunner moves up from high B tier to high A tier. Level 0-2 weren’t that improved, only having slightly increased health, but the faster speed and spawnrate means it is a bit less tedious as an early-game defense. Level 3 now has a way longer time to shoot at enemies before dying, but Level 4 and 5 got the biggest buffs. Their DPS was significantly improved, and the airstrike ability is super helpful for hordes of enemies, and they do actually quite a lot of single-target DPS. It is way more practical and very worth to use now, as it is good throughout all stages of the game, it really only struggles against major/final bosses. The removal of hidden detection sucks, but its ram damage can get most of the job done. As an additional indirect buff, invincibility frames for summoned enemies were improved, so units should no longer be instantly killed upon colliding with an enemy just summoned, so Military Base isn’t complete garbage against Breakers anymore. Military Base goes up from D tier to high B tier. The Beehive Grenade ability may seem like it’d be decent against hordes, but the explosion deals barely any damage and the DPS is still terrible. Placing multiple Swarmers does nothing since the bee damage doesn’t even stack. There’s pretty much no point in using it. It can spam guards but it has a long spawnrate of 45 seconds, and most fallen/molten games are not that long. Usually the maximum amount of time is 30 minutes, which is incredibly rare. Plus, by the time you have a golden perk, you probably have the meta towers capable of washing away enemies with ease in a short time, thus not allowing GCB to reach its full DPS. Plus, its DPS is quite inconsistent because if you're going to use it late-game, its guards usually die due to stuns or collision. I honestly prefer the old Golden Crook Boss compared to this new one. I miss the times when it could deal massive amounts of DPS with its minions. #4 - The Golden Scout Yes it is indeed better than The Golden Crook Boss for a number of reasons. Unlike GCB, it doesn't have a placement limit, is much cheaper, and has more range, allowing it to deal a lot of damage to enemies before they get out of GS's range. Plus, Golden Scout is now frequently used in speedrunning strategies because it is easier to get than Gladiator.. It can deal 36.96 DPS for only 6,325. Adding on to that, it can cost 5k with DJ, and it can be boosted with Commander. Allowing it to deal with the first 29 waves with ease which gives you plenty of time to farm for Accels/Engineers/G Mini guaranteeing that triumph, and it is the second best speedrunning tower in TDS. All of this for 5k-6k is too great of a deal to sacrifice. Definetly in the Top 5 early game towers, and a great speedrunning tower. #3 - The Golden Pyromancer Just.. wow! I didn't see Below buff a tower this much since the early days of the game. This thing went from being the worst to one of the best which is great! This is the 2nd best early game tower in the game. This thing melts and shreds early game enemies. You only need 1 of these to carry you to Wave 10! Golden Pyro also has pierce, allowing it to deal even more amounts of DPS! This is the best choice for ALL special gamemodes and events. It also melts defense, allowing your main-DPS towers to deal the full damage that their stats show. Enemies like the Nuclear Guardians and Fallen Guardians and Cavalry become a joke when Golden Pyromancer steps in the battle. This is now among the best towers in the game. Try pairing this with other golden perks or Accelerator and see how powerful Gold Pyro really is. Also, this can be a great sub-DPS, it can deal 60-80 DPS for 14k. Oh, and don't forget about elapsed damage! While it deals 40 less elapsed damage than Swarmer (3rd best event tower), it still deals quite alot of elapsed damage (80). This is overall a great golden perk. #2 - The Golden Cowboy Soloing hardcore is impossible! Nah, its possible. Lol stop capping. Look at this video by WitherStar. HOLY! HOW! verified_top_matches.snippet: Part 28 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 NEW TOWERS Executioner - Unlocked from beating Night 4 of the event, mechanics totally not copied from Clash Royale, the Executioner attacks enemies by throwing its axe, which will then travel to said enemy and damage it, which bounces to other enemies. Any enemy that is in Executioner’s range can be targeted. The amount of bounces depended on the upgrade. It was also one of the very few ground towers at the time to have flying detection, so it was usable as an early game tower for Hardcore. Anyways, the tower’s main purpose was crowd control. With how weak the other pure splash towers were at the time, the Executioner was by far the best crowd control tower. It may have been expensive to upgrade, and has bad single target DPS, but that’s not what it’s used for. It had a placement limit of eight. It lands a solid spot on mid-B tier. After nearly 2 years since its release, the developers finally caught on to Swarmer’s power, because of how many people abused its cheap but extremely high DPS on Night I and Night II. Unfortunately, this is a huge nerf. It makes it so much harder to actually stack bees, you would need to have multiple enemies around with some not stung yet to actually stack bees now, which is super unreliable. Goes down from mid S tier to low B tier. With how cheap level 3 Pursuit was to get, only costing a total of $3,650 for 23.11 DPS pre-nerf. It would make the Clankers, a lead enemy at Night IV, a complete joke with how much damage Pursuit’s missiles dealt. Pursuit was really nerfed just for that. Shotgunner has very high damage on a single shot, reaching over 100+ damage in only 1.5 seconds on max. During the grind for Shotgunner, the only mode you want to play is Molten. No exceptions. Molten is by far the best and the 2nd best for grinding coins and EXP. Molten gives 4x more than Normal and is way easier than Normal mode. When you are ready to start grinding for Shotgunner, do not USE SNIPER. Sniper is overpriced and does the same DPS as Scout, which is way cheaper than Sniper. Because of how terrible Sniper is, you are better off spamming Scouts to deal with the early waves and for the first slow boss. You are unlikely to die on Mystery waves, so do not count on RNG to save you. Once you reach 2500 coins, your next objective is to get Farm. Farm is by far the most required tower in the entire game (Events do not give any money, so do not bring it when you are doing events), being more useful than Cowboy. Since you have Shotgunner, grinding will be much easier, as you can reach Wave 40 if you get enough Shotgunners to deal with the zombies. Once you get Farm, your next objective is to get Dj Booth and Commander. This will allow you to solo Molten with no problem, which makes it so that once you reach the Molten Boss, you will not have to micro your towers to the back. Getting Commander and Dj Booth will not be as simple, as you will have to get them in 3+ hours since they cost 7500 if combined. Once you get Commander and Dj Booth, you will enter the middle game, where you will have to start grinding for levels and coins. During this time, you should get Ranger, Military Base, Minigunner, Turret and Ace Pilot. This will allow you to prepare for Hardcore, which is required for grinding Accelerator and completing the mode itself. During the grinding, the towers you want to get first will be listed in an order, with one being the first should be priortized first. Ranger Golden Crook Boss > Golden Scout > Golden Cowboy > Golden Pyromancer > Golden Soldier. Once you get Golden Minigunner, Golden Scout and Golden Crook Boss, do not grind for the last golden crates. They are not worth it unless you are doing challenges. After you have finished the entire game, you are in the End game, where you can carry noobs, do events, keep up with the community and just help others, and etc. IF this guide helped you, please comment. This post took over an hour to write. In a nutshell, you should get Shotgunner as your first tower, Farm, Supports, essential towers for triumphing Hardcore, Accelerator, events, Hidden Wave Badge, Pursuit, and Golden Crates. It was one of the mini updates of v1.6.3, which just added bugfixes. From this point on, the game mainly focused on rebalancing and reworking the towers, which was good.. But it would also severely start to power creep many unchanged towers. (that's unfortunately just how it works). BALANCE CHANGES Soldier Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $5,000 -> $3,500 Rocketeer Level 0 Cost: $850 -> $2,500 Damage: 8 -> 25 Firerate: 6.008s -> 5.008s Range: 16 -> 22 Deadzone Range of 12 added. Explosion Range: 4 -> 2.5 Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $350 -> $300 Damage: 8 -> 25 Firerate: 5.008s -> 4.008s Range: 16 -> 22 Deadzone Range of 12 added. Explosion Range: 4 -> 2.5 Level 2 Upgrade Cost: $600 -> $800 Damage: 8 -> 55 Firerate: 5.008s -> 4.008s Range: 20 -> 25 Explosion Range: 4 -> 2.5 Level 3 Upgrade Cost: $2,800 -> $6,500 Damage: 20 -> 100 Firerate: 4.508s -> 3.508s Range: 20 -> 25 Explosion Range: 5 -> 3.5 Hidden detection added Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $7,500 -> $18,000 Damage: 40 -> 225 Firerate: 4.508s -> 3.508s Range remains at 28 Explosion Range: 6 -> 4 After being useless for 2 and a half years, Rocketeer finally got a buff, a huge one at that. Its DPS, range and firerate were all improved. Its DPS at max went from 8.87, less than Paintballer, to 64.14! It also now has hidden detection after almost 4 years. The deadzone sucks, but Rocketeer’s huge range makes up for it and it's very manageable. Unortunately, the explosion range was made further smaller which hits 2 enemies at most, now having the same as Demoman. And honestly, the DPS still sucks for the cost, except for Level 2, which by far provides the best value. It also still has the 8 placement limit. Anyways, it can’t really be used for early-game because it’s too expensive, it’s best used for mid-game, spamming Level 2. It can be used for late-game, but there’s a lot better options. Rocketeer goes up from F tier, worst tower to low-B tier. Military Base Level 0 Starting Spawnrate: 20s -> 30s Well as if the starting spawnrate wasn’t already nerfed.. This nerf alone was kinda bad, but Military Base unfortunately became a victim of power creep of the early-mid 2023 balance changes, why? Many explosive towers were buffed, already having lead penetration, and other towers also got lead penetration for their main attack. Right now, Military Base’s main use is really just being the only reliable defense for Invisibles and Leads in early game Hardcore, which is now slowly diminishing. Moves down from low B tier to low C tier. Electroshocker Shock time is no longer proportional to enemy size, is now the same for every enemy regardless of size. It can now deal actual damage, albeit still bad for its cost, but it makes up for it by being able to hit multiple enemies, which it can now right off the bat! Now that it has flying detection, it also now has a niche at Hardcore mode, and it already had lead penetration, and it can still indirectly hit hiddens through its chain attack. It can hit so many more enemies now, so it also got much better at crowd control, and while the maximum shock time was nerfed, it used to be proportional to enemy size, so it couldn’t really stun larger enemies well. A global stun time of 0.5s plus 8 max hits is actually really solid. Electroshocker goes up from low C tier to high B tier. Ranger's use it extreme in mid game, as once you will have most likely placed multiple rangers with addition of Commander to do massive damage, shredding enemies in seconds. A downside of Ranger is how slow it shoots without Commander, allowing enemies such as Glitch or even Bolt to past by without even getting Ranger a hit on one of them. But still, it is a must bring in Hardcore and even Hidden Wave. Farm is your number 1 economy source for everything. First things first, farm is able to generate thousands of dollars at max if you properly farm and balance on defending and generating income. Farm is also a must bring, which you will expect 100% of any level 50s above will always bring farm unless they aren't aware of the new meta. Farm does not have many cons but is sure enough a tower you want to bring IMO. Gladiator is one early game tower that dominates everything even the Golden Minigunner and the Accelerator. Gladiator has the base damage of 2 for only 300$ and has splash, making it an incredibly effective early game tower and at late game. Gladiator not also becomes much stronger, but has some of the most versatile abilities over others. The frenzy allows him to chip away enemies with 12 DPS, which is incredible for a cost for only 2550$! Despite that, Gladiator's cheap cost for incredible DPS makes it an all round tower for all of the game. Gladiator's short range means that fast enemies will get past him but his firerate easily counters them even if the Bug or the Rusher gets in range. Definitely bring it in your deck. Golden Minigunner is another high dps tower but now has an improved damage boost to the Platinum Minigunner, which used to give 25% damage boost. Golden Mingunner is essentially your Minigunner except with an improved damage of 1 to 2 at Level 3 and 4. Golden Minigunner is also spammable, which means Golden Minigunner is an phenonemal alternative to Accelerator. A huge downside is how costly it is at early game, which means you are tempted to sell your farms to place down one at the cost of 2000$. A major downside is that it is affected by the infamous ROF bug, which means you are going to receive less than 120 DPS than the wiki says. Despite all of this, Golden Minigunner is definitely a tower to bring inside of Hardcore and multiplayer games. S- Ah yes, the Accelerator. Accelerator boasts one of the highest DPS in the game, only beaten by the unobtainable Mark 5. Accelerator not only has the highest damage but also has hidden detection which Ranger does NOT, which counters Ranger's weakness. Accelerator is also benefitted even more by the Commander, which boosts the Accelerator's buffed damage in DPS. There are so many downsides that keeps Accelerator from reaching S Tier, such as burst, ROF Bug, and charge up time. My strategy of course was to spam level 0s, this is because level 1 and 2 only slightly upgrade range and give HD, so spamming level 0s is the most cost efficient early game. I've run into problems with using the tower and I would like to compare it to another tower I have: the Golden Crook Boss. The Golden Crook Boss seems to do better in my experience and here is why: The first upgrade instantly doubles the damage, also one-shotting the quicks (or speedys I always get them confused) The second upgrade gives the golden crook, which is really good for dealing with the heftys on wave 7 and abnormal boss on wave 10 After getting level 2, I'm able to farm and get level 3 for wave 10 even in 4 player servers. Here are things the Golden Scout has going for it Somewhat better range More cost efficient at level 0 Can be placed instantly, unlike the Golden Crook Boss where you need to wait until wave 2 The problem I'm encountering is that by wave 7, Golden Scouts simply won't cut it. Now of course, I can just continue to spam these because of their insane cost-efficiency the moment they are placed, but there are problems with this. The most important issue: Space. Golden Scouts do have more range and more cost efficient DPS counting out the crooks and mafia of the Golden Crook Boss, but you can't just place all of them in the exact same optimal spot. Inevitably, some of them are going to have much worse range coverage than others placed in the same spot like the 3-4 turn coverage on Harbor Even with a decent amount of level 0s placed, they can't seem to deal with the heftys on wave 7 very well, and if I try to upgrade one for better damage I actually let a couple of enemies leak, especially on maps that don't have great spots to get optimal range coverage. The damage isn't a big deal, but keep in mind I want a good early game tower and the Golden Crook Boss only requires I leak on wave 1-3 depending on the amount of players (less income) and map. I don't see the Golden Crook Boss used for many strats, as the Golden Scout is a decently popular hidden wave tower, but the Golden Scout seems to only be good under heavily controlled circumstances, maybe even more so than the Swarmer. I want towers that can be good for the role I want it to do under almost any circumstances, but it seems the Golden Scout is only good if I get a highly optimal map and I pray that a teammate can place something good for wave 10. You can say it's just because I play with randoms, so on a true tier list Golden Scout might still be pretty high, but this just seems to be another scenario where a tower is worse on wifi due to certain mechanics like less income, less total towers for each player and the obvious fact that I'm not playing with experienced players, but most of my games of TDS are obviously not gonna be with professionals. So yes, to my surprise, I am somewhat disappointed by the Golden Scout. If I'm just using it wrong on wifi then let me know. It was most notable for adding the Krampus’ Revenge Event. It also added one new tower, and reworked/rebalanced all the towers with freezing capabilities (except Jester). Let’s dive in. NEW TOWERS Cryomancer - Unlocked from beating the Krampus’ Revenge Event, the Cryomancer attacks by firing a frost beam from its freeze ray, which slows down up to 3 enemies (6 enemies at max) by 5-10% per hit every 0.208s, maxing out at 50-75%. The slowdown lasts 2 seconds, then 6 seconds at Level 3-4. At Level 4, when an enemy is slowed down further at 75%, it gets frozen for 2 seconds. Cryomancer does have a limited amount of ammo, 40 at Level 0, 50 at Level 1, and 80 at Level 2-4. When it runs out of ammo, it will have to reload for 2s, it is not that much of a hindrance though, even with its short range. Cryomancer does not deal any damage until Level 2, where enemies hit now get dealt 1 damage every 0.25s as they are being slowed down. It also reduces the defense of enemies by 10% per tick, maxing out at 33%. All in all, Cryomancer is very powerful at stalling hordes of enemies, because of its very high slowdown. While its single-target DPS of 21.62 at max level is abysmal, it is a support tower, and it actually deals with hordes of weaker enemies fairly well. It unfortunately does not have hidden detection though, but it can indirectly hit hidden enemies through its beam. The Cryomancer lands a spot on high B tier, it would’ve been A tier in my opinion if it had hidden detection. BALANCE CHANGES Freezer Now applies a chill slowness effect when hitting an enemy, only freezing them when they are further slowed down than the maximum slowdown. Now drops defense every tick while an enemy is slowed down or frozen instead of dropping it on hit. Level 0 Cost: $350 -> $450 Damage: 0 -> 1 Firerate: 3.008s -> 0.608s Burst Count of 1 added (Cooldown of 0s) Range: 8 -> 10 Freeze Time: 0.8s -> 1.5s Slowdown per shot of 15% added Maximum Slowdown of 45% added Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $350 -> $150 Damage: 0 -> 1 Firerate: 3.008s -> 0.608s Range: 10 -> 12 Freeze Time: 1.35s -> 1.5s Slowdown per shot increases to 20% Maximum Slowdown increases to 60% Level 2 Upgrade Cost: $400 -> $625 Damage: 0 -> 2 Firerate: 3.008s -> 0.608s Range remains at 12 Freeze Time: 1.35s -> 1.5s Defense Dropping: 0% -> 10% (Maximum: 20% -> 33%) Level 3 Upgrade Cost: $1,400 -> $1,625 Damage remains at 2 Firerate: 3.008s -> 0.128s Burst Count increases to 4 (Cooldown of 1s) Range remains at 12 Freeze Time: 1.35s -> 2s Slowdown per shot increases to 25% Maximum Slowdown increases to 75% Defense Dropping: 5% -> 10% (Maximum: 20% -> 33%) Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $2,500 -> $5,000 Damage: 2 -> 3 Firerate: 1.508s -> 0.128s Burst Count increases to 7 (Cooldown of 1s) Range remains at 14 Freeze Time: 1.35s -> 2s Slowdown per shot increases to 25% Maximum Slowdown increases to 75% Defense Dropping: 5% -> 10% (Maximum: 20% -> 33%) Frost Grenade ability added - Throws a grenade with a 6 explosion radius that freezes up to five enemies for 6 seconds. Cooldown of 25s. Level 5 removed Freezer finally got its long-awaited rework after being useless for several years. Its stalling capabilities obviously got massively buffed, as well as its DPS, which is still bad but it’s a support tower anyway. Multiple Freezers, with no placement limit can stall tons of enemies when set on Random targeting, and you also have its Frost Grenade ability to come in clutch, and it also now finally has hidden detection. Unfortunately, for Freezer, the newly added Cryomancer pretty much does the same job as Freezer but better. Freezer still does have its advantages though, such as its ability and hidden detection. Freezer moves up from F tier, the worst tower to low-mid B tier. Frost Blaster Placement Limit of 10 added. Now slows down enemies after they thaw. Now fires a piercing projectile that can hit multiple enemies at once Defense dropping is now tick based when an enemy is frozen or slowed down instead of dropping it on hit. Level 0 Cost: $300 -> $850 Damage: 1 -> 2 Firerate: 3.008s -> 0.858s Range: 10 -> 12 Freeze Time: 0.4s -> 0.5s Slowdown of 30% added (Slowdown Time of 2s) Max Hits of 3 added Projectile Speed of 60 added Lead penetration added Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $350 -> $300 Damage: 1 -> 2 Firerate: 3.008s -> 0.758s Range: 13 -> 12 Freeze Time: 0.4s -> 0.5s Hidden detection added (moved from Level 2) Level 2 Upgrade Cost: $600 -> $950 Damage: 2 -> 4 Firerate: 3.008s -> 0.758s Range remains at 14 Freeze Time: 0.4s -> 0.5s Defense dropping: 0% -> 10% (Maximum: 20% -> 33%) Increases Max Hits to 4 Level 3 Upgrade Cost: $1,500 -> $3,500 Damage: 15 -> 10 Firerate: 1.508s -> 0.758s Range: 14 -> 16 Freeze Time: 0.5s -> 0.75s Defense dropping: 5% -> 10% (Maximum: 20% -> 33%)
