I'll always have a spot for Golden Crook Boss, not only because of his extremely good cost efficiency for most levels, and because of the minions they spawn. You can always get the job done with GCB, as his minions clear up practically everything. However, his main weakness, is his placement limit of 4. This is their worst weakness, as after you've placed only 4 of them, you already have to place another tower to get more DPS. This results in them being more like a support tower than anything. And also, major bosses' stuns usually result in all of their minions dying, which makes them lose so much DPS. I could see GCB becoming way better if the placement limit for them was increased to something like 6 or 7 though. #3 or 4 : Golden Minigunner This is the most controversial ranking by far. Now, Golden Mini is by far the most solid late game out of all these towers (it's also really good). However, the firerate bug is a really big issue with GMini. It's 23.2k for 120 DPS, but it only has 103 DPS with the bug. It's also a good replacement for Accelerator if you don't have them. I feel really bad for placing GMINI here. (it's interchangeable with GS) I really can't justify placing them at the 4th spot either, but they're really good at what they do. #3 or 4 : Golden Scout Golden Scout is probably the most versatile early game tower. He's extremely cost efficient (just spam level 0s) at all levels, and can be used for early game and late game. He can basically defend any single early game wave whether in Molten/Fallen/Event as long as you upgrade and spam him properly. $6.3k for 36 DPS? Worthwhile. He can also, be used to speedrun (though of course, Gladiator's always better) #2 : Golden Pyro: One of the best early game to late game options. He's very all rounded : he can deal with swarms well, reduces defense (kinda niche though), has base hidden detection, and cost efficient at all waves. He's good at all modes, even including Hardcore where he can be used to defend the early waves, penetrate leads, and reduce defense. He might struggle with bosses a little, but to be honest, GP is always used as a support tower though , as when have you seen him be spammed as a main DPS? #1 : Golden Cowboy : The most all-rounded tower of all of the golden towers. Has good DPS at all levels and, well, he's basically a farm that deals damage. That's enough explanation on why he's practically one of the best towers in the game, as farms themselves are already good, but a farm that actually deals decent damage? Just spam him and he's way more efficient than a simple farm. He's good for all modes, and even needed to solo Hardcore. (im getting lazy here so i dont feel like typing another 10 sentences on why gc is the best golden tower) To be honest, you can swap Golden Mini and Golden Scout here. The only thing good about it is its range, which is the highest out of any ground tower, and that’s about it. #35 - Hunter: Hunter is not a terrible early game tower per chance at its lower levels, it also has decent range, but the problem is, upgrading it is not just not worth your money. #34 - Militant: Militant may be used for early game, but the problem is, its ammo and reloading system is such a huge hindrance to the tower, made even worse by its terrible range. Its DPS is so bad that it has less DPS than Medic. #33 - Medic: Medic practically has no use now as its Cleansing ability is bugged. Even with the prior buff, Rocketeer was still bad for single-target, except for the Level 2 upgrade. The explosion range buff means it can now hit up to 3 enemies at max, which does give it a DPS of 179.61, assuming all 3 enemies get dealt full damage. Overall, Rocketeer did get slightly buffed, but Mortar and Executioner are still better for crowd-control. Mortar Level 0, 1 Damage: 10 -> 12 Explosion Range: 8 -> 5 Level 2 Damage: 20 -> 24 Explosion Range: 12 -> 6.5 Level 3 Damage: 50 -> 55 Explosion Range: 14 -> 6.5 Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $9,500 -> $8,500 Damage: 100 -> 125 Explosion Range: 14 -> 7 Level 5 Upgrade Cost: $23,000 -> $21,500 Damage: 175 -> 250 Explosion Range: 20 -> 8 This rebalance aims to make Mortar more focused on single-target, but in cost, it halved or more its explosion radius. This is really dumb because you don’t really use Mortar for single-target, even then, it’s single-target DPS is still bad for its cost. An explosion radius of 8, which is actually just slightly less than it has in the present day, is still decent for crowd-control, but overall, this rebalance was just really dumb. Mortar goes down from mid-high A tier to low A tier. Pursuit Level 0 Damage: 2 -> 5 Firerate: 0.108s -> 0.258s Level 1, 2 Damage: 3 -> 8 Firerate: 0.108s -> 0.258s Level 3 Damage: 4 -> 5 Firerate: 0.083s -> 0.093s Hidden detection removed Level 4 Damage: 7 -> 8 Firerate: 0.083s -> 0.093s Level 5 Damage: 12 -> 13 Firerate: 0.083s -> 0.093s Basically, Pursuit got higher damage in turn for slower firerate, which did actually slightly improve its DPS at Level 0-4, making it slightly better for mid-game. Level 5’s DPS did go down from 174.57 to 169.78, which is very marginal for a late-game tower. The removal of hidden detection is a bummer, but Pursuit already had full stun immunity, flying detection, and lead penetration, so it’s really not that bad. Pursuit stays at the same spot in A tier. Kinda pointless rebalance honestly. Engineer Level 0 Firerate: 1.508s -> 1.258s Range: 14 -> 12 Max Units: 2 -> 1 Level 1 Firerate: 1.508s -> 1.258s Range: 15 -> 14 Max Units: 2 -> 1 Level 2 Firerate: 1.508s -> 1.258s Range: 16 -> 15 Deadzone Range: 3 -> 2 Max Units: 2 -> 1 Level 3 Upgrade Cost: $1,600 -> $1,750 Damage: 8 -> 10 Firerate remains at 1.258s Range: 16 -> 15 Deadzone Range: 3 -> 2 Max Units: 2 -> 1 Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $3,500 -> $3,250 Damage remains at 15 Firerate remains at 1.008s Range remains at 18 Deadzone Range: 3 -> 2 Max Units: 3 -> 2 Level 5 Damage: 25 -> 30 Firerate remains at 1.008s Range remains at 18 Deadzone Range: 3 -> 2 Max Units remains at 3 Level 6 Upgrade Cost: $35,000 -> $33,500 Damage: 40 -> 45 Firerate remains at 0.808s Range remains at 20 Max Units: 4 -> 3 This rebalance aimed to make Engineer less reliant on sentries, so they made the Engineer itself deal more DPS, but now it builds sentries, which actually just reduced its combined DPS throughout, except for Level 5. The deadzone range really just means it can’t place sentries way too close to itself. Anyways, just skipping to the most devastating nerf of all, Engineer’s combined DPS went from 454.5 to 359.44 because it now builds 1 less sentry, which is a huge nerf, but it is still by far the highest raw DPS in the game. But remember, these sentries are units, so they cannot be affected by support buffs, only the Engineer itself gets affected. I actually did the math for this, but with this nerf, 6 Engineers now deal a total DPS of 2,156.64, with Commander’s 55% firerate buff, it only goes up to 2,337.72, because the sentries are not affected by buffs. Let’s look at Accelerator. Its charge-up, cooldown and burst time actually do not get affected by firerate buffs, but its tickrate does. 8 Accelerators deal an average DPS of 1,666.4, which does fluctuate over time. With Commander’s 55% fierate buff, it goes up to 2,500, higher than 6 Engineers with firerate “buffs.” Accelerator’s stun vulnerability problem is solved by a Medic, but Engineer also appreciates Medic to make its sentries’ shields always be around (correct me if im wrong for the math). So, in conclusion? Accelerator does go back to being better than Engineer, and Engineer is now ranked much lower on S tier. TOWER RANKING: F T

This update was the re-release of the disastrous Hardcore BETA Update launch, but there were a few slight differences between the two. The most notable changes are some towers got renamed (and reworked for the worse), and some towers had their maximum level reduced to Level 4. However, even with an additional 2 months, the update still felt rushed. There were quite a lot of rampant bugs, and most notably, this is when the game went into a delay era where the balance was an all time low with so many weak towers. This was honestly one of the hated updates in the game’s history, and honestly rightfully so. Anyways, I won’t be going as in-depth with the patch notes since I uncovered pretty much all of these already, but I will be stating where there was a difference or not than the patch notes from Hardcore BETA. If you want a more in-depth review and description of the miscellaneous changes, new towers and balance changes, here’s the post about Hardcore BETA. https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000292548/r/4400000000001773062 MISCALLENEOUS CHANGES Just the same as Hardcore BETA. Look at the original post for the changes. NEW TOWERS Accelerator Golden Soldier Sentry and the 3 Platinum Skins (except Plat. Crook Boss) remain removed, alongside that, Mecha Base was back to being staff-exclusive. It was broken as hell in bugs and stats anyway. (Due to the sheer length of the post, I could not cover the entire post in here, so the patch notes will be on the replies yet again.) TOWER RANKING: F TIER #38 - Paintballer: Paintballer has horrible DPS for how expensive it is, bad range, and the explosion radius is so small that it may just be a single target tower. There’s pretty much no point in using it. #37 - Sniper: Sniper has practically the same DPS as Scout for 2-3x the cost, making it really bad. The only thing good about it is its long range and that’s it. E TIER #36 - Freezer: Freezer has bad range, and it can’t even freeze and stall enemies that effectively, especially larger enemies with the freeze time becoming lower as the enemy becomes larger. It’s just useless. #35 - Rocketeer: Rocketeer fires extremely slowly, is insanely expensive for how low the DPS is, and the explosion radius is way too small to make up for that, the damage is way too low, so it can’t even handle crowds. It also has a placement limit of EIGHT. #34 - Demoman: Demoman has bad range and terrible DPS for how expensive it is, the explosion radius is so pitifully small and it doesn’t even have hidden detection #33 - Hunter: Hunter is not a terrible early game tower per chance at its lower levels, it also has decent range, but the problem is, upgrading it is not just not worth your money. #32 - Slasher: Slasher, being a melee tower, has terrible range. Even then, its DPS isn’t that good for its cost, which is very detrimental for a melee tower. The Knife Throw passive is also really weak, dealing very minimal damage #31 - Frost Blaster: Frost Blaster at Level 0-2 is extremely weak, with Level 3 only being the somewhat decent level, even then it’s not that good. Level 4 and 5 are a scam for their cost, you can’t even use it for support since the freeze time is really short. So it sucks both at offense and support. D TIER #30 - Scout: Level 0 Scout is actually not that bad for their cost, and can somewhat handle the first few waves of Normal and Molten Mode. The upgrades don’t provide that much for their cost though, with Level 4 being the only somewhat decent upgrade. #29 - Soldier: Soldier was surprisingly effective at Levels 0 and 1, being cheap and spammable for early game. However, upgrading it past that was pretty much pointless and a waste of money. DESTROY THIS GAME. How’re we gonna do that? By completely destroying players! verified_top_matches.title: why I think There is no best golden skin
verified_top_matches.snippet: Small note: I lost my old account (hihihi99) so this is my new account So you probably hear of golden skins. If you haven't played tds for 2 years or something, golden skins are skins from golden crates that give buffs to towers, like damage. Every golden skin has its unique buff that differs it from the other golden skins and making it better than the original tower. However, you probably also hear of something like this: Golden minigunner is the best golden skin! or Golden soldier is the best golden skin!. Personally, I don't think there is any best golden skin, since there is no golden skin thats amazing at everything and is op from waves 1-40. For example, lets take golden minigunner. Golden minigunner might be a good mid-late game tower, but im pretty sure you can't get it on wave 1 and you will have to leak alot and maybe even die before affording it. Another example could be golden scout. It does excel at wave 1-9, but golden scout is never going to be able to handle the last waves of fallen mode unless you spam it real bad until the placement limit and then fallen king comes and wrecks you on the last wave instead. In conclusion, every golden skin is good at its own thing (yes even golden pyromancer since he can reduce defense of enemies on fallen mode) and there isn't really a best golden skin unless your talking of the best golden skin in a very specific scenario. Bes

I’m going to uncover some miscellaneous changes first. MISCALLENOUS CHANGES Firerate Bug/ROF Bug - What even is the Firerate Bug? It is a bug that slows down the firerate of every tower and unit by 0.05s (0.025s for Level 4-5 Minigunner for some reason), prior to the Overhaul Update. This significantly affected fast-firing towers like the Minigunner, Ace Pilot and Turret. According to the wiki, the Firerate Bug has existed since the very release of the game. However, I just don’t think this was the case in Pre-MEGA, and early MEGA. It really only took notice around early 2020, but I have chosen to finally take the ROF Bug into account on these lists, since as mentioned, it started to take notice around this time and couldn't really be ignored anymore. This drops towers like the Minigunner (and Golden), Turret and Shredder on the ranking. Shield - This was a new mechanic that was added that enemies could have. This included the Templar, Summoner Boss and Fallen King. Basically, it visually made four shields appear around the enemy, which made the enemy limit most forms of damage to whatever the quoted number on the shields. Exceptions were: All forms of damage from units, including collision and ranged (for example, the Golden Mafia and Railgun Tank). Burn damage from the Pyromancer. Splash Damage. This addition significantly affected slow firing towers, especially Outlaw. However, for some reason, splash damage completely bypassed it, so there was an all time high demand for Rocketeer and Mortar for Fallen Mode. This really doesn’t move down Outlaw a placement on the ranking, as it is still the uncontested best late-game DPS tower with this addition. Rocketeer gets moved up from B tier to S tier, and Mortar moves up from B tier to high A tier. Also this meta change suddenly made Farm extremely vital and necessary for everything now, despite the other forms of cash generating still being the same. It goes from C tier to S tier. BALANCE CHANGES Crook Boss Level 0 Cost: $600 -> $650 Level 1 Cost: $275 -> $300 Level 4 Cost: $4,000 -> $4,500 Level 5 Cost: $8,500 -> $9,000 The cost increase on the early levels aren’t really that much, as Level 3 Crook Boss is still a very dirt cheap upgrade for the DPS. This moves base Crook Boss down from B tier to C tier, and Golden Crook Boss from S tier to A tier. Electroshocker Level 0 Range: 9 -> 7 Level 1 Range: 11 -> 9 Level 2 Range: 13 -> 11 Level 3 Damage: 10 -> 6 Range: 15 -> 11 Chain Range: 8 -> 9 Level 4 Damage: 22 -> 10 Range: 15 -> 11 Chain Range: 8 -> 9 Level 5 Damage: 40 -> 22 Range: 19 -> 15 Chain Range: 8 -> 9 Don't really know what the point of this nerf was, since the tower was perfectly fine. Anyways, the range nerf is quite a bummer, chain range was barely increased, the damage nerf might seem a lot but that's not what the tower was used for anyway. It can still stun-lock most enemies. Goes down from high B tier to low B tier. Holiday Archer Arrows now do less damage as they pierce through enemies. Arrows now pierce through a limited number of enemies. This is quite a big nerf to the tower, making its early levels, Level 0-2 very weak. It's still solid in mid-game, still being able to do lots of DPS for its cost on its later levels, the massive range is still there, and max hits of 7-8 is a lot. Goes down from high A tier to low B tier. Military Base Level 5 - Railgun Tank Health: 800 -> 1,200 What the tower really needed was to make it worth upgrading past Level 2. It did gain a niche to “counter” shielded enemies as its ram damage did bypass the damage cap, but it is very inconsistent at doing so it will mostly just ram a different enemy. Does go a few placements up in C tier though. Demoman Level 0 Cost: $550 -> $450 Firerate: 3.3s -> 2.55s Level 1 Cost: $200 -> $100 Firerate: 3.3s -> 2.55s Level 2 Cost: $500 -> $400 Firerate: 3.3s -> 2.55s Level 3 Cost: $1,350 -> $1,000 Firerate: 3.3s -> 2.55s Chain Range: 8 -> 9 Level 4 Firerate: 2.3s -> 2.05s Level 5 Damage: 38 -> 32 Firerate: 1.2s -> 1.3s This “buff” really doesn't change anything. The cost decrease is barely anything, and the DPS increase is very marginal. Level 5, the only somewhat decent upgrade before, was nerfed. The cost decrease doesn't make up for the DPS loss. The tower stays at the same spot as it is in D tier.
